segments.label: Global Travel & Security
segments.monitors: State Dept. travel advisory levels, active conflicts, terrorism, civil unrest, kidnapping, and security conditions affecting Southwire personnel and business travelers worldwide.

items.title: Mexico Level 3 sustained; cartel violence in border states
items.body: State Dept. Level 3 advisory remains in effect for Mexico, with Do Not Travel (Level 4) designations for Tamaulipas, Sinaloa, Colima, and Guerrero. Cartel activity along the Monterrey-Laredo corridor is elevated. Southwire employees traveling to Mexico operations should follow pre-approved routes and check in with security teams before departure.

items.title: Iran conflict spillover raises risk across Middle East corridor
items.body: US-Iran tensions following the Hormuz ceasefire collapse have elevated travel risk across Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen, and the broader Gulf region. Several airlines have suspended service. Personnel with travel to the region should defer non-essential travel and maintain contingency evacuation contacts.

items.title: China Level 2 advisory: exit restrictions and business traveler risk
items.body: The State Dept. Exercise Increased Caution advisory for China remains active. Chinese authorities have imposed arbitrary exit restrictions on foreign nationals involved in business disputes. Personnel traveling for sourcing or vendor visits should notify legal and ensure no active commercial disputes exist with counterparties before arrival.

items.title: Honduras Level 2: gang activity and violent crime in urban areas
items.body: Honduras maintains a Level 2 advisory. Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula continue to report elevated homicide and extortion rates. Business travelers should use vetted ground transportation, avoid night travel outside secured areas, and coordinate with local operations security contacts.

priority.detail: Level 4 (Do Not Travel) for Tamaulipas, Sinaloa, Colima, Guerrero. Cartel violence and kidnapping risk elevated in border states. Exercise extreme caution and avoid non-essential travel to Level 4 states.

Arbitrary enforcement of local laws including exit bans. Risk of wrongful detention. Heightened surveillance of foreigners. Business travelers should notify legal counsel of travel and ensure no active disputes with Chinese entities.
Violent crime including murder, armed robbery, and kidnapping are common. MS-13 and other gangs are active. Use vetted ground transportation and avoid traveling at night outside secured areas.
No significant safety concerns for business travel. Normal precautions apply. Monitor for rare labor disruptions at border crossings that can affect cross-border freight.

Political protests can occur with little notice in Santiago and other cities. Some demonstrations have turned violent. Araucania region has elevated tension related to indigenous land disputes. Monitor local news.

segments.label: Southwire Industry
segments.monitors: Southwire-specific competitive intelligence, commodity inputs, supply chain, customer demand signals, travel security, M&A, and leadership action items.

items.title: Copper supply tightening; spot price at 14-month high
items.body: LME copper at $5.94/lb driven by China smelter output cuts, Peru mine disruptions, and tariff-driven U.S. import demand pull. At current levels, unhedged wire COGS exposure is significant. ERM recommends confirming hedge book coverage through Q4 and initiating a repricing review for contracts indexed to spot.

items.title: Ocean freight rates at 22-month high; no relief before mid-September
items.body: Drewry WCI composite at $4,166/FEU, up 5% WoW. Asia-US West Coast rates are hardest hit. Southwire's imported raw materials and finished goods logistics costs are directly exposed. Supply chain team should confirm whether inbound shipments are on spot or contract rates and whether buffer inventory is sufficient to absorb a 6-8 week delay scenario.

items.title: Prysmian signals accelerated U.S. grid cable investment
items.body: Prysmian completed acquisition of a U.S. fiber cable startup and announced an expanded Clarksburg, WV manufacturing line targeting utility grid upgrades. This positions Prysmian directly against Southwire's grid hardening segment. Competitive intelligence team should assess whether this changes 2027 contract renewal posture with utility customers.

ma.title: Prysmian / fiber cable startup acquisition
ma.body: Prysmian completed acquisition of a U.S. fiber cable manufacturer; announced integration with General Cable's grid division. Move accelerates Prysmian's position in DOE GRIP-funded utility projects directly competing with Southwire's transmission cable segment.

ma.title: Nexans eyes North American cable consolidation
ma.body: Nexans CFO commented publicly on evaluating bolt-on acquisitions in U.S. low-voltage wire. No announced transaction; monitor for competitive displacement in residential market.

horizonWatch.title: NEC 2026 code cycle – copper minimum gauge requirements
horizonWatch.body: NEC code cycle may tighten minimum gauge specs, favoring heavier-gauge copper over aluminum substitutes. Southwire benefits if finalized.

horizonWatch.title: Copper futures backwardation signal
horizonWatch.body: LME forward curve moving into backwardation above 12 months. Historically precedes supply shortfall. Hedge desk should assess roll strategy.

horizonWatch.title: FERC Order 881 – grid hardening mandate
horizonWatch.body: FERC transmission planning requirements will drive $50B+ in utility wire and cable demand 2026-2031. Southwire DOE positioning is a strategic priority.

horizonWatch.title: EV charging infrastructure cable demand
horizonWatch.body: NEVI program funding flowing. DC fast charger installations driving demand for 480V and 600V cable. Southwire EV product line should be front-of-mind in bid cycles.

horizonWatch.title: AI data center power density increase
horizonWatch.body: Hyperscaler next-gen AI training clusters require 2x-4x more power cabling per rack vs. prior generation. Custom cable spec discussions underway with major cloud providers.

actions.title: Brief VP Supply Chain: Hormuz disruption impact on copper import lanes
actions.body: US-Iran ceasefire collapse and Hormuz re-escalation is adding $800/FEU surcharges and 4-day avg delays on Asia-originated copper rod shipments. Supply chain team should confirm whether inbound copper inventory is sufficient to cover a 30-day transit disruption and whether spot sourcing from domestic rod suppliers is available at current basis.

segments.label: Geopolitics
segments.monitors: Conflict zones, sanctions regimes, export controls, and treaty shifts affecting Southwire's supply chain and international operations.

items.title: US-Iran ceasefire collapses; Hormuz shipping contested
items.body: A temporary US-Iran ceasefire agreement collapsed over the weekend after Iran resumed uranium enrichment above 60% purity. IRGC naval units are conducting harassment operations in the Strait of Hormuz. Approximately 21% of global LNG and 17% of global crude transits the Strait. Ocean freight surcharges have spiked $800/FEU on Asia-origin lanes.

items.title: Taiwan Strait tension: PLAN drills increase in frequency
items.body: PLA Navy conducted its third live-fire exercise near Taiwan in six weeks. U.S. Indo-Pacific Command has repositioned carrier assets. Taiwan Strait disruption would affect semiconductor supply chains and is a macro escalation signal relevant to Southwire's end markets and global risk posture.

items.title: Section 301 tariff review expanded to include wire and cable components
items.body: USTR has confirmed the Section 301 review will cover finished wire and cable from China in addition to existing copper rod tariffs. Comments period closes August 15. If tariffs on finished wire are imposed, it could relieve price competition in the domestic market but increases cost pressures on any Southwire imported inputs.

segments.label: Military Activity
segments.monitors: Troop movements, naval operations, airspace closures, and escalation signals in regions relevant to Southwire's sourcing and logistics corridors.

items.title: Pentagon deploys additional carrier strike group to Persian Gulf
items.body: USS Harry S. Truman carrier strike group ordered to the Persian Gulf following Hormuz ceasefire collapse. Combined with USS Gerald Ford already on station, this represents the largest U.S. naval presence in the Gulf since 2003. Shipping risk is elevated for the next 30-60 days regardless of diplomatic outcome.

items.title: Red Sea reroutes persisting; Cape of Good Hope adds 11 days avg transit
items.body: Houthi attack frequency has declined from Q1 highs but has not stopped. The majority of container lines continue to route via Cape of Good Hope rather than Suez, adding 10-12 days to Asia-Europe and Asia-East Coast U.S. transit times. Southwire should assess whether any inbound shipments are affected.

segments.label: Supply Chain & Freight
segments.monitors: Ocean freight rates, port disruptions, rail and trucking capacity, cargo theft, and logistics bottlenecks affecting wire and cable input materials.

items.title: Drewry WCI at $4,166/FEU — 22-month high, no near-term relief
items.body: The Drewry World Container Index composite hit $4,166/FEU, up 5% WoW. Asia-US West Coast rates are the largest driver, with the Shanghai-LA leg at $5,210/FEU. Analyst consensus sees no meaningful rate relief before mid-September, after peak season blanked sailings resolve.

items.title: Port of Savannah at 88% capacity; chassis shortages developing
items.body: Georgia Ports Authority reported Savannah at 88% capacity amid import surge. Chassis pool availability has tightened, and dwell times are extending. Southwire shipments routed through Savannah should be monitored; consider diverting time-sensitive loads to Charleston or Houston.

items.title: Cargo theft: wire and cable theft up 18% YTD; copper targeted
items.body: CargoNet Q2 2026 report shows cargo theft incidents up 18% YTD. Wire and cable represent 22% of targeted cargo categories, a 6-point increase over 2025. FBI has confirmed organized theft rings operating on the I-10 corridor targeting copper wire loads. GPS tracking compliance and high-value shipment protocols should be reviewed.

segments.label: National Weather
segments.monitors: Severe weather events, flooding, extreme heat, hurricanes, and winter storms affecting Southwire facilities, transportation routes, or end-market construction activity.

items.title: Midwest heat dome threatens grid stability and distribution ops
items.body: A high-pressure heat dome is forecast to cover the central U.S. through July 20 with temperatures reaching 105°F+ in Kansas City, St. Louis, and Chicago. Grid stress events are possible. Southwire manufacturing facilities in the region should confirm cooling redundancy and have demand response protocols ready.

items.title: Above-average 2026 Atlantic hurricane season forecast upgraded
items.body: NOAA upgraded its 2026 Atlantic hurricane season forecast to 'extremely active' (20-25 named storms). Peak season runs August-October. Southwire Gulf Coast operations, PVC resin suppliers (OxyChem on the Gulf), and port routes through Houston and New Orleans should be in business continuity scope.

segments.label: Markets
segments.monitors: Equity markets, commodities, interest rates, credit spreads, and macro signals relevant to Southwire's cost structure, customer demand, and capital planning.

items.title: Housing market contraction signaling end-market demand risk
items.body: Housing starts fell 3.1% MoM to an annualized 1,284K units, well below the 1,400K threshold associated with healthy residential wire demand. NAHB builder confidence at 38 (below 50 neutral). With 30-year mortgage rates at 7.24%, residential wire demand is expected to remain suppressed through at least Q1 2027.

items.title: Fed holds rates; no easing signal before Q4
items.body: The Federal Reserve held at 4.50-4.75% at the July FOMC meeting, with chair commentary indicating data dependency before any rate cut. No clear pathway to easing before Q4 2026, which sustains pressure on construction borrowing costs and delays customer CapEx authorization timelines.

segments.label: National News
segments.monitors: Federal legislation, regulatory rulemakings, tariff policy, labor law, and infrastructure spending directly affecting the wire and cable industry.

items.title: Senate moves IRA clean energy buy-domestic provisions to reconciliation
items.body: Senate leadership confirmed that IRA domestic manufacturing content requirements for clean energy projects will be preserved in the reconciliation package. This sustains preference for U.S.-produced wire and cable in utility and renewable energy procurement. Southwire's IRA positioning should be maintained.

items.title: OSHA proposes updated heat illness standard for manufacturing
items.body: OSHA published a proposed rule on heat illness prevention in outdoor and indoor workplaces. Manufacturing environments with sustained temperatures above 80°F would require engineered controls and acclimatization protocols. Southwire should assess compliance readiness across facilities, particularly in Alabama and Georgia during peak summer.

segments.label: Social & Human Capital
segments.monitors: Labor market conditions, union activity, workforce trends, DEI regulatory shifts, and social risk factors affecting Southwire's talent and operating license.

items.title: NLRB unfair labor practice rulings increasing; manufacturing sector on alert
items.body: The NLRB issued three significant ULP rulings against manufacturing employers in Q2 2026, tightening standards on union communication and pre-election conduct. Southwire's labor relations team should review organizing activity monitoring and ensure manager training is current on NLRB compliance.

items.title: DEI program rollbacks under executive scrutiny; federal contractor risk
items.body: Federal contractors and recipients of federal infrastructure funds face heightened scrutiny on DEI programs under current executive priorities. Southwire's exposure as a supplier to federally funded grid projects warrants a compliance posture review with legal and HR.

segments.label: AI Industry & Security
segments.monitors: AI regulatory developments, cyber threats using AI tools, critical infrastructure attacks, and industrial AI adoption affecting Southwire's risk profile.

items.title: CISA issues advisory: AI-enabled ransomware targeting critical infrastructure OT
items.body: CISA issued an advisory warning of a new AI-assisted ransomware campaign specifically targeting operational technology environments in manufacturing and utilities. The variant uses AI to map OT network topology before deploying payload. Southwire IT and OT security teams should verify ICS/SCADA segmentation and patch status immediately.

items.title: AI Act (EU) enforcement scope may affect Southwire international operations
items.body: The EU AI Act begins enforcement of high-risk AI system requirements in August. Southwire's European-touching operations and any AI tools deployed in safety or hiring contexts may fall into scope. Legal review recommended before Q3 end.

segments.label: Tech News
segments.monitors: Semiconductor supply, grid technology, energy storage, industrial IoT, and EV demand signals relevant to wire and cable end markets.

items.title: AI data center power density driving outsized cable demand
items.body: Hyperscalers' next-generation AI training infrastructure requires 2x-4x more power cabling per rack than prior-generation data centers. Morgan Stanley estimates $14B in incremental cable spend 2026-2028. Southwire's data center cable product line should be in active bid discussions with hyperscaler procurement teams.

items.title: NEVI EV charging funding releasing; cable demand follows
items.body: DOT confirmed $1.2B in NEVI Formula Program funds releasing to states in Q3. DC fast charger infrastructure requires specialized 480V/600V cable. Southwire should confirm sales coverage of state NEVI grantees and their primary electrical contractors.
